translation:
...the owner of the site, Rambhai, built his own house there in its memory. In it he has kept his household shrine of daily worship at that very spot. Thus this is a historic site, and so it is a place of sacred merit.

Aritha

When Bhagat Haribhai of Aritha came to Shahpura to meet Jivanji Maharaj, Jivanji Maharaj was sitting under a mahuda tree in his own field, holding satsang (holy company). There, in the height of summer, a field of val-papdi (a bean crop) stood green — how could that be? Jivanji Maharaj said that it had turned green for the sake of the saints. This same Haribhai had a field in Aritha which had likewise turned green. In memory of this, this field in Aritha is known as the val-papdi field, a sacred ground. The devotees there have built a temple to Shivji in that field. This urge to raise such a temple is a consequence of the polluted climate of the present age. As Kabirji has said:

_Shaligramku shila par patku, Brahmaka katu shir |_
_Shivjiko sukhri lagadu, Vishnuku pahuchau shunya ||_
(I would dash the shaligram stone against a rock and cut off Brahma's head; I would smear Shivji with something to leave him writhing as though with an itch, and send the three-natured Vishnu off into the formless void.)

Kabirji is saying that he would smear Shivji with something so as to leave him restless with an itch — as if rubbed with something maddening — that he would cut off Brahma's head, and that he would send the three-natured Vishnu away into the formless void: such is Kabir's saying. So the raising of a Shiva temple in the field that carries Jivanji's memory is a result of the influence of this age; but this village, with its field of val-papdi, remains a sacred place of merit.

The samagam record states that in Samvat 1709, on Vaishakh Sud 5, Haribhai came from Aritha to Shahpura, and Vaishnav Jivanjidas himself went to the field, along with all the Vaishnavs. They went to the field and saw a great abundance of growth (rasayan) there. Then Haribhai said, "Vaishnavji, this is Vaishakh — high summer — where has this lush growth come from?" In reply it was said that this is the word of Bhagat Bardaoli —

_Dharati ambar aade dei ane ravi rashi pani pavan ||_
_Sant jaan e to rachi nahintar karan kavan ||1||_
(The earth, the canopy of sky, the sun, the water, and the wind — know that it is the saint who has fashioned these; otherwise, what other cause could there be?)

This is the word of Parashuram:

_Gaau santan ke karane | Hari varsavat meh |_
_Take pichhe Parashuram | Duniya paale deh ||1||_
(For the sake of the cow and the saints, Hari sends down the rain; and because of that, Parashuram sustains the bodies of the world.)

_Gau santan bhukhe mare | Duniya lapalap khay |_
_Ta karan the Parashuram | Suka pad pad jay ||2||_
(When the cow and the saints go hungry while the world eats greedily, it is for that reason that Parashuram lets the land turn dry and barren.)

From the wording of this samagam it is said that Jivanji made the growth green in the field at Shahpura; but if we also say that he made the val-papdi field green at Aritha, confusion arises. The explanation for this, from the handwritten manuscript (hasta likhit granth) no. 98, page 29, is as follows.

As an illustration of how the growth was made green at Shahpura: it is like a person who irrigates with water from a well to make a garden, in which other grasses and the like also grow. Using this illustration, in a mystic (samadhi) idiom, to explain its true purpose, it is written that:

"The one who owns the well is the Lord of Grace (Kripanath); the saplings are the saints; the wild grass and undergrowth are the world — this growth was made for the sake of the saints." This manuscript no. 98 records, regarding the growth God made for the saints, the following account:

Question Two

Ram Kabir, Question Two — the village of watermelons. In Shahpura, Vaishnav Jivandasji resides. In Samvat 1709, on Vaishakh Sud 5, Vaishnav Haribhai came from the village Aritha. He came to the field. There the Vaishnav brought and set out the growth (rasayan). "Bucha, Maharaj — how did this growth come about, in the month of Chaitra?" When the Vaishnav asked this, Vaishnavji said: there is a well; from it a garden has been made; there are many saplings in it, and within it countless wild grasses and undergrowth are nourished. This is only an illustration — the principle to be understood is that the growth was made for the sake of the saints.

Thus, regarding Jivanji at Shahpura, the above is what is written in the handwritten manuscript no. 98, pages 29 to 31. On reflection, it appears that when Haribhai came from Aritha to Shahpura, it must have been in the heat of summer, in a month such as Vaishakh, and watermelons were being offered to the devotees to eat; these watermelons must have been grown by him in his own field named Vadiya, that...
